sections.content:
This lesson reviews three ways to look back at something that did not happen. You know all of them.

• *Ojalá* + pluperfect subjunctive, from B2 Unit 16: *Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.*
• *Si* + pluperfect subjunctive, from B1 Unit 35, and *de* + *haber* + participle, from B2 Unit 10: *De haberlo sabido, habría venido* means *Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido*.
• *Debería haber* + participle, from B2 Unit 10: *Debería haber llamado.*

One detail is worth fixing in your mind: in *de haberlo sabido* the pronoun goes after *haber*, joined to it: *haberlo*, *haberte visto*. It never goes before *haber* or after the participle.

items.english: I wish I had studied more.

items.spanish: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido.
items.english: If I had known, I would have come.
Had I known, I would have come.

items.spanish: De haberte visto, te habría saludado.
items.english: Had I seen you, I would have said hello.

sections.content: All three look at the past and all three are about something that cannot change any more. The main clause after *de haberlo sabido* uses *habría* + participle, never the future.
